rationale: The module-surface and FFI shapes the 2026-10-03 ontology census measured on the whole corpus (14,066 admitted .hs files, production parseFile). Three defects, each pinned here, each with a corpus number in the analyzer's source comments: (1) 392 of 54,830 `exports` edges carried a KEYWORD or keyword phrase as the exported name — 100 `type`, 32 `data`, 8 `pattern`, the rest `pattern <Ctor>` / `type <Ty>`; (2) 1,040 of 1,153 `foreign_import` entity texts are QUOTED string literals and the quotes were published, so `references c_keepCAFsForGHCi -> "keepCAFsForGHCi"`; (3) 409 `module_export` re-export nodes were dropped entirely by `if (expNode.type !== "export") continue`. Plus one adjudication: a self-named superclass (`class Recursive a => Recursive a`, legal under UndecidableSuperClasses, present in GHC's own testsuite at T11254.hs:12) is not published, because a self-named edge is a self-loop in symbol-ID space — the same rule the `contains` post-loop already applies — and it was the only `extends` row the F5 oracle disagreed on. The fixture covers every export SHAPE the pinned grammar produces (31,892 export nodes: 6,697 with a name child, 24,515 a bare variable, 43 a bare keyword whose name sits in a sibling ERROR), so it pins the case rather than one instance of it.

expectRelationships.comment: the ordinary `Widget(..)` form: the TYPE is what the module exports; the constructor list is a visibility detail, not a second name
export -> variable: a plain lowercase name
`type WidgetId` — the KEYWORD is in a `namespace` child and the name in a `name` child. Published as `type WidgetId` before this fix: a target no source file declares.
`type (&&)` — prefix_id -> operator. Published as `type` before this fix (the text cut at the first paren). The operator spelling is what the module exports.
`data Gadget` — the grammar mis-parses this entry so the export node's only named child is the keyword `variable("data")` and `Gadget` lands in the sibling ERROR. Recovered.
`module Data.Gadget` — a RE-EXPORT, its own grammar node type (`module_export`), and 409 of them corpus-wide were DROPPED because the reader only accepted `export`.
the C entity is a string LITERAL, so the grammar's entity text is `"widget_alloc"` WITH its quotes. 1,040 of 1,153 corpus FFI entities are quoted literals and the quotes were the published endpoint.
the same callee from TWO sites. The site line is part of the dedupe key, so these are two edges at two lines — the pair is pinned so a per-set regression cannot collapse them unnoticed.
a NON-self superclass: the positive half of the rule the next forbid pins from the other side.

a PATTERN SYNDICOME publishes a constructor-shaped symbol owned by the module, so the `exports Data.Surface -> :|` row above has a target. The M14 runner caught the gap: `export(s) [":|"] do not resolve to a top-level symbol`. Corpus: 1,094 pattern_synonym nodes over 261 files, 94 export entries naming one.

forbidRelationships.comment: the KEYWORD, not a name. 100 corpus-wide.

the KEYWORD, not a name. 32 corpus-wide.
the keyword PHRASE. The name is WidgetId; the qualifier is not part of it.
the keyword PHRASE. ~250 of the corpus's 392 keyword targets are `pattern <Ctor>`.
a Haddock comment in an export list is not a name (the M60-HK class: 39 such edges corpus-wide)
the QUOTED literal. The spelling a reader greps for in the C header is widget_alloc.
the quoted header name in the shape-C FFI form

a self-named superclass is legal Haskell (UndecidableSuperClasses; GHC's own testsuite/tests/typecheck/should_compile/T11254.hs:12) but a self-loop in symbol-ID space is not an edge, and it was the ONLY extends row the F5 oracle disagreed on — 1 UNEXPLAINED of 98 over a 1,200-file stride draw.

the signature half and the equation half are ONE declaration. Two contains edges at two lines for one name would be the multi-clause-function defect `processFunction` already collapses; the O(1) index does the same here.
